item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02105","case1_error":"Treats the 12-apple excess as the entire green-apple count, omitting the additional 16 green apples.","case2_error":"Assumes equal parent counts per group and discards the remainder, reducing the correctly calculated 50 parents to 48.","reason":"The first mistakes a difference for a total; the second imposes an unsupported distribution and drops remaining people.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02106","case1_error":"Equates current practice with half itself, ignoring the 20-day accumulation relation, then unjustifiably concludes two days.","case2_error":"Provides correct formulas for total candies and packs, but appends unsupported 20 instead of 11.","reason":"The first explicitly introduces false relations; the second gives an incorrect final number without showing any erroneous evaluation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02107","case1_error":"Adds 12 to depth for '12 feet higher,' instead of subtracting it.","case2_error":"Uses Rudy's 10 mph speed for Grayson's second leg instead of the stated 20 mph.","reason":"The first reverses the directional relation; the second substitutes another person's speed into an otherwise correct distance calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02108","case1_error":"Counts the two mother lambs again even though they are already included in the original six.","case2_error":"Evaluates the correctly written sum 9 + 9 + 9 + 8 + 8 + 8 as 49 instead of 51.","reason":"The first double-counts existing animals; the second makes a numerical evaluation error in a correctly constructed sum.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02109","case1_error":"Sets Roger's current experience equal to his retirement target, replacing the given constraint that Tom has twice Robert's experience.","case2_error":"Confuses individual and team rates, computes time as half a rate instead of its reciprocal, and incorrectly simplifies the expression.","reason":"The first conflates a future target with a current value; the second mishandles work rates and the rate-to-time relationship.","judgment":"different"}]}
